sources.locator: 3.1 Macroscopic Design, state recursion and output equations
excerpts: Given an init random state, the model repeatedly applies the core block R, which accepts the latent state and the embedded input and outputs a new latent state.
After finishing all iterations, the coda block processes the last state and produces the probabilities of the next token.
sources.inspection: The same core R is reapplied for i=1,...,r; the head uses the final state. This supports variable repeated computation as a mechanism, not a guarantee of improved answers with every extra round. The course finite-class head and event tasks are its own proposed design.

sources.locator: Introduction; TypeSafe primitives; Atomic questions, composed in code
excerpts: Jev evaluates typed questions against a state and returns structured results directly.
You get typed values and probability distributions that your code can branch on, sort by, and route with.
Choice: Choose an option from a list; Score: Score the state on a rubric; Noul: Is this statement true? noul (0–1).
sources.inspection: The three public contracts support service choice, rubric grading and a truth probability interface. The introduction does not give an internal training recipe, and no proprietary architecture or calibration-performance claim is inferred. C is the course planned finite-domain service.
